title: Sauchie man appears on BBC show to discuss 'UFO sightings' in central Scotland
excerpt: Mysterious lights, unexplained sightings and tales of the unknown have taken centre stage on a new TV series.
content:
Sauchie's Malcolm Robinson appears on BBC show Mythland

Malcolm Robinson (middle) with hosts Zara Gladman (left) and Evelyn Hollow. (Image: Supplied)

This article is brought to you by our exclusive subscriber partnership with our sister title USA Today, and has been written by our American colleagues. It does not necessarily reflect the view of The Herald.

Wee County paranormal investigator Malcolm Robinson has appeared in a new BBC Scotland show about UFOs.

Mythland looks at historic unexplained incidents across the country, with the Sauchie man featuring in episode two.

The half-hour piece explores an area that became known as the “Falkirk Triangle” for a period in the 1990s due to a large number of mystery objects that were said to have been spotted in the sky there.

Asked by co-host Zara Gladman why he thinks it’s seen as a hotspot, he said: “This is the million-dollar question, I wish I knew the answer to that.

“All we can safely say is that the people of Bonnybridge are seeing objects that do not conform to conventional aircraft.”

“What people have been seeing since 1992, is triangular-shaped craft, balls of light dropping down from the sky, they’ve seen structured craft, like two soup plates joined rim-to-rim.

“Our aim is just to gather as much information as possible and find out what’s real and what’s not real.”

The programme is currently available on iPlayer, with other topics covered including witch trials in Fife.

Malcolm has recently called for an inquiry into “UFO activity” over Scotland, but it was rejected by the UK Government.

He has published a long list of books on the subject, along with others such as poltergeists and monsters.
